title: Leviticus
author: Moses is traditionally understood as the author of Leviticus as part of the Pentateuch.
date: Traditionally connected with Israel's wilderness period after the giving of the law at Sinai.
audience: Israel, especially the priests and the covenant community, teaching them how a holy God is to be approached and worshiped.
historicalSetting: Leviticus takes place largely at Sinai after the tabernacle has been established. It gives instructions for sacrifices, priesthood, purity, holiness, feasts, and covenant living.
themes: Worship ordered according to God's command
keyVerse: Leviticus 19:2 — "You shall be holy; for I, Yahweh your God, am holy."
christFocus: Leviticus points to Christ through the sacrificial system, the priesthood, the Day of Atonement, and the call to holiness. Jesus Christ is the perfect sacrifice, the greater High Priest, and the only One through whom sinners may draw near to God.
outline: Holiness in worship and life — Leviticus 17-22
Feasts, covenant blessings, warnings, and vows — Leviticus 23-27
